newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN AUG LONG-TERM PRIME LIKELY UNCHANGED-TRADERS.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN AUG LONG-TERM PRIME LIKELY UNCHANGED-TRADERS.

text.p: Japan's August long-term prime rate is likely to be left unchanged at 2.7 percent, bond traders said Friday.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd is scheduled to announce its long-term prime rate next Monday afternoon.
The prime rate, at which long-term banks lend to their most creditworthy customers, was cut by 0.2 percentage point to 2.7 percent in July.

The IBJ usually sets its long-term prime rate 0.9 percentage point above its five-year debenture coupon rates. The IBJ's July five-year bank debentures, with a coupon rate of 1.8 percent, were being traded at 1.65 percent on Friday afternoon.
Some traders said there was a slight possibility that the IBJ could lower its long-term prime rate by 0.2 percentage point should its bank debentures be traded at this level on Monday morning.

"Although the IBJ usually does not change its long-term prime rate unless there is variation of 0.2 percentage point between its five-year debenture coupon and the traded price, there is the chance that it could change it this time in the face of expectations that bonds may continue to be strong," one trader said.
